sources.citation: Nuuttila OP, Nummela A, Korhonen E, Häkkinen K, Kyröläinen H. Individualized Endurance Training Based on Recovery and Training Status in Recreational Runners. Med Sci Sports Exerc. 2022;54(10):1690–1701.
sources.design: Matched-pair randomized parallel endurance-training intervention after preparation
sources.publication_check: Bibliographic record and original article text independently inspected via indexed PMC and publisher passages; journal-layout PDF text consulted. Direct PMC/DOI re-open and figure screenshot failed. Complete Figure 1 graphical branches, supplemental materials, notices and correction/retraction audit remain outstanding.
sources.rights: CC BY 4.0 stated in original article; metadata, links and original factual summaries only pending intended-use rights review.
sources.appraisal: Forty recruited; seven dropouts and three excluded finishers. Final treadmill sample PD 14, IND 16; final 10-km sample PD 13, IND 16. Comparator baseline-scaled with scheduled volume/interval changes. Adaptive multivariable bundle; minimal concurrent other exercise. Verified key protocol and endpoint text, not complete algorithm or missing-data behavior. Results versus Discussion HIT count discrepancy requires review. No component effect or hybrid transfer established.

claims.assertion: In the analyzed recreational runners, the multivariable individualized program improved 10-km running time more than the baseline-scaled predefined program from T1 to T3.
claims.limitations: Forty recruited; seven dropouts and three excluded finishers, one additional PD endpoint unavailable. Endpoint n=13 PD and 16 IND. Small bundled intervention, possible post-randomization selection and test timing/freshness differences; very little other training. No isolated effect of a marker or adjustment rule.
claims.assessment: Original Results and Figure 3 caption verified in article text. Promising direct recreational running comparison with limited precision and hybrid applicability; independent review and complete protocol/notice checks outstanding.

support.locator: Methods Participants and Study protocol; Results Performance and laboratory tests, Fig. 3 and accompanying text, T1 to T3
support.result: IND −6.2 ± 2.8% (n=16), PD −2.9 ± 2.4% (n=13), mean ± SD; between-group ES 1.23 (95% CI 0.42–2.02), p=.002; group-time interaction p=.006.
support.restriction: Six-week volume and six-week interval periods after preparation; analyzed endpoint only, not an intention-to-treat estimate established here. No individual marker attribution, dose rule, or approved hybrid transfer.

claims.assertion: Both programs improved maximal treadmill speed from T1 to T3 in the analyzed recreational runners; the between-group contrast was uncertain.
claims.limitations: Same small trial as the 10-km endpoint, not an independent replication. Endpoint n=14 PD and 16 IND; post-randomization losses/exclusions; protocol-specific treadmill outcome and little concurrent other exercise. Interval permits a range of effects; no equivalence test.
claims.assessment: Original Results text and Table 3 context inspected. Between-group estimate is from Results prose rather than within-group Table 3 effect sizes. Independent verification and transfer review outstanding.

support.locator: Methods Participants; Results Performance and laboratory tests, T1 to T3 between-group contrast in prose and Table 3 context
support.restriction: Maximal speed of incremental treadmill protocol, not race performance or VO2max; no component attribution or approved hybrid transfer.
